pages.quiz:
PHYSICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Dynamics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Dynamics.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Dynamics.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Dynamics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Dynamics.

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin lenses? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thin lenses.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Thin lenses.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin lenses.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin lenses.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mains electricity? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mains electricity.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mains electricity.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mains electricity.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Mains electricity.

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Floating and Sinking? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Floating and Sinking.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Floating and Sinking.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Floating and Sinking.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Floating and Sinking.

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 0 °C

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Photoelectric effect? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Photoelectric effect.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Photoelectric effect.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Photoelectric effect.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Photoelectric effect.

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

12. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Photoelectric effect and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Electromagnetic induction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Mains electricity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Transistors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Dynamics.

2. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin lenses.

4. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mains electricity.

5. C — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

6. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Floating and Sinking.

7. C — 100 °C

8. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Photoelectric effect.

10. D — Ice melting to water

11. C — Producers

12. A — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Photoelectric effect; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Mains electricity; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Transistors; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
